title: Flute
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS flute (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: One head-joint pull, nothing retuned per note, leaves D4 at -15.4 c from equal temperament and A5 and G6 at +17.3 and +29.9 c. Every note is too clean, with too little breath noise, and its harmonics miss the recording's. In the scale and melody E5 splits. G4 and C5 start flat. The flute is the printed Pearl PF-661 (Dickens 2007, Listing B.15), hole terms on, slide out 13.2 mm, one set of lengths on every note. The player is one flautist's printed pressure, jet length and lip opening per note (de la Cuadra's thesis); C5 has no printed row and takes the midpoint of B4 and C#5, and G6 takes Fletcher 1975's medians. The jet is computed, a forced Bickley jet driven by the pipe's own sound; A5 speaks in its second register and G6 in its third. The aim was the printed flute and equal temperament, not the recording.
physics_present: The printed Pearl PF-661 flute (Dickens 2007, Listing B.15) as one tone-hole network on every note, with the slide out 13.2 mm, one length for every note, solved once against equal temperament and never against a recording (the only figure printed for this flute at A440 is 8 mm, p. 106)
Printed hole terms on every hole: key cups (eq. 2.30 + 0.1 a, eq. 2.32 where perforated), key pad into closed holes (eq. 5.4), matching length, inner radiation and the series term

One flautist's printed blowing pressure, jet length and lip opening for each note (de la Cuadra thesis Fig. 3.4). D4, G4 and A5 follow that player's printed pressure within the note, then hold its median, and D4 also has the same player's printed breath onset, which G4 and C5 borrow, scaled to each note, because the print has no other. C5 has no printed row: midpoint of B4 and C#5, flat after that start. G6 is past that table: Fletcher 1975's medians over four players, 1254 Pa (band mostly +-50 %) and 4.33 mm (band about +-20 %), with the lip opening and width borrowed from the A5 row, flat after a 50 ms attack

The blow's wander after the printed columns, on the D4, G4 and A5 pages and the scale and melody stops with room for it: its size comes from one player's slurred scale (de la Cuadra 2005 Fig. 3.4, player FA), read off a figure at 8 Pa per pixel, and nothing above about 21 Hz can be seen in that figure
A forced Bickley jet driven by the pipe's own sound, with the Kutta exit and laminar Bickley widening across the mouth

Jet momentum drive (Thwaites and Fletcher 1983, Eq. 1, kappa 1). On the D4 and G6 pages only, it is taken across the jet's own Bickley velocity profile instead of as one lumped flow, which takes 2.0 to 3.1 dB off the term's fundamental there. On G4 and C5 that form takes 2.9 and 3.1 dB off it in the first 0.35 s, and from 0.4 s the note sounds its octave, so those pages keep the lumped term. A C5 render with the lumped term and the station cut width that the profile form brings keeps its register to the release, so the jump is the profile's. A5 keeps its page and the lumped term
The jet's velocity and source term on the embouchure's open strip (hole length x lip opening); the mouth's other terms stay on the mouth area

The jet's swing limit (Fletcher 1976, time form this model's) and one jet width in the cut and the swing (Fletcher and Douglas 1980, Verge 1995, Auvray et al. 2014), on the D4, G4, A5 and G6 pages and every note of the scale and melody. C5's own page carries neither row and says why
Breath noise from the turbulent jet (Verge 1995), on above Re_h 700, in a Butterworth band at the cited in-band level

The embouchure radiating from its solved window (on the five note pages and the scale and melody stops that radiation's memory is stepped exactly with the flow held over each step, 27631e7a4), under a rigid one-sided lip whose open strip narrows with the note (Coltman via Fletcher 1975), with a rigid half-plane for the player's face just behind the lip's edge

Open holes and the foot radiating through compact baffled loads (on the five note pages and the scale and melody stops the foot's reaction is an unflanged pipe end's, Garcia Mayen 2021 Eq. 14 with Silva et al. 2009, and it is still heard as baffled), summed with the embouchure at a receiver 1.524 m above it on the five note pages and the scale and melody stops: the collection's 5 ft, borrowed, because Iowa's flute page prints no distance and its bassoon and trumpet pages, recorded in the same anechoic chamber with the same Neumann KM 84, print 5 feet. On the D4 and G4 pages the foot and the open holes also hear each other free-field, after the travel time between them, in the card's flat plane and without the mouth (`outlet_mutual free-field`)
A warm, moist bore gas from Coltman's measurement on a played flute, with room air outside the instrument

Fractional-delay propagation on every section, and viscothermal loss on the bore sections over a limited band, on the five note pages and the scale and melody stops including main-bore sections 7 and 12, which carried none before, and on every page but G6 and on every stop each open-hole chimney (on the five note pages and the scale and melody stops its memory is stepped exactly with the flow held over each step, adbb97dbb and f78078db2)

Separated flow at every opening, on the five note pages and the scale and melody stops: the flow leaving each open hole and the foot's open end separates and loses its kinetic energy, a loss in series with each opening's own radiation (`opening_losses`, Δp = ρQ|Q|/(2(C_c A)²)). C_c is 1 on every opening: the open end as Atig, Dalmont and Gilbert 2004 print it (C. R. Mécanique 332:299-304, Eq. 3, c_d = 2 for a thin-walled unflanged end), the side holes at the row's ceiling of 1, a loss 1.2 times the one Dalmont et al. 2002 print for a sharp-edged hole (Acta Acust. united Ac. 88:567-575, K_h = 0.5, as quoted by Szwarcberg et al. 2024, JASA, Sec. III.2.1, which is C_c 1.096): a C_c above 1 would be pressure recovery, which this row's full-head loss cannot represent. With it every graded page ties on the grader's count (D4 10 of 14, G4 9 of 14, C5 11 of 14, G6 11 of 15; A5 has no ruler), the pitch moves 0.03 c or less on the pages and 0.04 c or less on the stops, and no harmonic from H2 to H12 re H1 moves more than 0.7 dB

The player's airway ahead of the flue (`upstream_airway`, landed as 07dc291d4e), on the C5, D4 and G4 pages: Story's measured vocal tract for /u/ (2008, Table I, 44 sections, lips first) ahead of the Weibel 1963 subglottal tree to 24 generations, with the voice cards' yielding wall on every tube. Each sample the airway's port gives the flue's foot pressure in closed form; the airway's resistance to steady flow (5.287e4 Pa s/m^3 in the receipt) holds the foot below the blowing pressure, and those notes sound 0.30 to 0.80 c lower than without it. The airway and the pipe exchange no waves: the jet's speed depends only on the foot pressure. Since ad2f27d055 the row carries `two-way` on these pages: where the open-circuit pressure at the flue is not positive, on 28097 to 42058 samples of the 288 kHz clock (30 runs on each), in the attack and after the release, the last at 2.075 to 2.365 s, the flue draws air back by its own law, signed, with the forward coefficients, a stand-in: no print gives the law of air drawn back between a flutist's lips, or the loss where it enters them. The most air drawn back is 6.68e-6 to 1.55e-5 m^3/s, and drawing it back deepens the least open-circuit pressure at the flue to -171.1 to -402.4 Pa (one way -69.6 to -87.4 Pa). The air drawn back comes from outside the lips at ambient pressure, the airway stays filled with the source gas and the mixing has no model, and a sample that draws air back has no jet. One way, the flue passed no flow on 7557 to 12796 samples (64 to 70 runs), the last at 2.006 to 2.265 s. The count ties on all three (C5 11 of 14, D4 10 of 14, G4 9 of 14). With `two-way`, against the one-way flue on the same binary, all three tie again at those counts.
physics_missing: The right pitch. One pull can't close the spread: D4 is flat at -15.4 c, and A5 and G6 stay sharp at +17.3 and +29.9 c; the momentum drive's profile form brings D4 up 5.7 c and costs G6 5.7 c. Their recordings read -7.5 c and +12.3 c, and G6's is 11 c under it. The stops of the scale and melody play -1.8 to +12.0 c. The pull is 5.2 mm past the only figure printed for this flute at A440, and a flutist would get part of that flattening from the lip and face, which this card doesn't carry. G6 also speaks about 1000 Hz in its first 50 ms and is on the note by 100 ms. From D4 to C5 this flute spreads about 15 c, as the recordings do (16 c), and players on this same flute spread about 24 c (Dickens Fig. 7.2, as read here). What's left has no printed term that can go on a card: Dickens' eq. 7.2 is fitted to the flutists' pitch, so it isn't used

Harmonics like the recordings'. The largest misses through H8, dB re the first against the recording: D4 H8 -38 against -26, G4 H2 -11 against +2, C5 H2 -21 against -6, A5 H3 -4 against -31, G6 H7 -56 against -25. G4 trades one hole for another: the cut's own second harmonic vanishes when the jet spends half of each cycle on one side and its third when it spends a third, and no render so far has both H2 and H3 right. G4's H3 is that hole. One listening point can swing a single harmonic a long way, because the mouth and the holes can arrive nearly equal and nearly opposite at one point and not at another: between 1 m and 1.524 m above the embouchure, on the same flows, G4's H6 goes from -33 to -15 dB re the first and A5's H3 from -30 to -5, so no one harmonic should be read as the instrument's physics. The receiver sits at the collection's 5 ft, borrowed. There the mean miss over H2 to H12 falls on D4 (8.9 to 7.4 dB) and G4 (10.0 to 6.7) and rises on C5 (5.4 to 6.8) and A5 (5.6 to 7.9)

Breath noise at the right level. Harmonics-to-noise reads above the recording on every note: D4 34.6 against 28.5 dB, G4 37.8 against 30.9, C5 35.6 against 32.3, A5 28.3 against 27.3, G6 36.8 against 22.6. On D4 and G4 the openings hearing each other raised it 1.2 and 1.7 dB. G6's is the largest gap on any flute page; the part that has been read is that H1 outgrows the noise. The blow's wander barely touches this. The cards keep the source's level from a recorder-like pipe (Verge 1995), and nothing found prints a level at this flute's jet length and lip opening, so no gain was set for it

A printed start from rest on any note but D4. G4 and C5 borrow D4's, scaled to each note: the attack comes inside the ruler, but the note starts flat, -26 and -29 c from equal temperament in its first 100 ms, within 5 c of where it holds by about 0.25 s, dipping about twice as far as the recording. Tried on A5, it speaks on A4 for about the first 0.12 s, so A5 keeps its authored 50 ms attack, as do G6 and the scale and melody, whose stops mostly have no room for it

A measured lip jet: the jet's response is computed from a Bickley profile, the jet card on the cards is an estimate (authority X-Est), the labium offset of 0.29 mm is from another player (Onogi), and the mouth contraction of 0.6 was measured on a recorder's mouth (Auvray et al. 2014, Table I), not an embouchure. A jet card measured on a rig fed by blowing pressure was tried in place of the estimate and refused itself. At Re about 148 the rig's tone locks at 0.31 to 0.79 times Brown's stage-I edge-tone law and moves 52 % when the rig is a quarter longer. With an absorbing layer at the outlet the two lengths lock within 9 % of each other, but the jet slows to Re about 93 and locks at 0.62 to 0.68 times the law. No cause is named

A printed area for the jet's momentum term. The printed law names the pipe's cross-section and says nothing about a chimney; the cards use the embouchure chimney's area, because on the pipe's area every note tried jumps toward the octave. Removing the steady momentum part doesn't bring H4 down to the real on any note
The player's real face, lip and lip plate: the lip and face are rigid stand-ins at set positions

Radiation beyond compact baffled loads: the cards' receiver band ends at 2.8 kHz, below the highest harmonics the pages read, the holes sit in a flat baffle plane rather than on the tube. On D4 and G4 the foot and the open holes hear each other free-field, after the travel time between them (`outlet_mutual free-field`), but the tube neither shadows nor scatters what passes between them, and no term carries the mouth's sound to the holes or the foot; with it those two pages tie on the grader's count and come out cleaner and flatter (harmonics-to-noise up 1.2 and 1.7 dB, pitch down 0.84 and 2.07 c on the served clips). Tried on C5 and G6, the same row scored one fewer (11 to 10 of 14: the odd/even balance 9.39 to 11.96 dB against a ruler of 11.71) and two fewer (11 to 9 of 15: harmonics-to-noise 14.14 to 15.27 dB against a ruler of 14.67; spectral flux 0.89 to 0.95 dB against a ruler of 0.90) and lowered their pitch 2.59 and 0.92 c, so those pages keep the openings apart, as do A5 and the 17 scale and melody stops, which the grader does not count. A computed baffled row in which every opening loads every other was tried on G4 and refused before rendering: at orders 24, 26 and 28, the most the 256-state limit allows, its fitted matrix missed the 2 % allowance (2.46, 2.22 and 2.01 %). Openings that hear each other weighted by their own radiation (`outlet_mutual pritchard`: the free-field term between every pair scaled by the square root of the two openings' own radiation resistances over a free-field monopole's, Pritchard 1960 as printed by Butler 2022, Eq. 1), which all six recorder stop pages carry, was tried on 2026-11-09 on the four counted pages, added on C5 and G6 and in place of `free-field` on D4 and G4, and refused before rendering on each: the resistance matrix of the openings, their own loads plus the mutual term, had no Cholesky factor at some frequency of the check that admits the row, every 5 Hz from 5 Hz to Nyquist. These cards' holes take the baffled load and only the foot the unflanged pipe end's, where every recorder opening takes the unflanged one. The exact matrix is passive by construction; where on the grid the check failed is not printed. At the bottom of the grid the exact matrix of these openings in a line is singular to double precision: its smallest eigenvalue over a unit diagonal is 1.4e-18 at 5 Hz on D4 and 4.0e-18 at 500 Hz on G4, under the 2.2e-16 of rounding, as on the recorder's F5 stop (3.3e-25 at 50 Hz), which passed; there the verdict turns on departures of the realized terms from the exact ones far below anything audible. Each live card, rendered beside on the same binary, reproduced its live clip byte for byte, so D4 and G4 keep `free-field` and C5 and G6 keep the openings apart

Viscothermal loss above the cards' band, and any in the riser (4.4 mm) or the pad-closed hole chimneys (1.89 to 2.38 mm): each quarter of a loss cell must span at least one sample of travel, 4.8 mm at the cards' 288 kHz, and they are shorter. G6's open-hole chimneys carry none either: a G6 render with their loss scored one fewer on the grader than the posted one
Wall and pad vibration, vibrato, slurs and tonguing. The scale and melody are one note card per slot, joined, each with its own attack and release
One player's row at G6: its pressure and jet length are medians over four players (Fletcher 1975), and its lip opening and width are A5's

Two notes of the scale and melody don't hold as printed. A4 leaves its note within 3 % of its held 478 Pa, or within 5 % without the pull, both well under the 539 Pa the same player printed on this note, so its 0.5, 0.6 and 1.2 s slots start flat at 478 Pa instead of on the printed track, and this card's first register is narrower than the player's. E5's stop splits: its waveform repeats at half the pitch, with a line at half the pitch 7 dB under the note, a line at 1.5 times the pitch 4 dB over it and one at 3.5 times the pitch 5.7 dB under it

The player's airway (`upstream_airway`) on the G6 and A5 pages: tried on 2026-11-09 with the tract, tree and wall the C5, D4 and G4 pages carry. G6 loses one measure (11 to 10 of 15 inside the ruler, and 11 to 10 by the strict): spectral flux over time grows from 0.872 to 1.029 dB, out of the ruler. Its flue passes no flow on 17610 samples in 72 runs, the last at 2.278 s, after the release at 2.2 s, and its open-circuit pressure falls to -1702 Pa against the 1254 Pa it is blown at. A5 has no ruler to count on. Both stay without the row.
